title: Chapter 202: Third Building, 13th Floor
html:
Uncle Wong nodded. It took him a moment to collect himself. “When the elevator opened, I nearly died of fright. My mind went blank.”

“And then? Did the white shadow attack you?”

“She fled the instant she saw me, and to this day I don’t understand how she ran without making a sound!” Uncle Wong’s gaze kept drifting toward Chen Ge’s phone. He plainly wished to forget the memory.

“Could panic have kept you from noticing her footsteps? Even someone running barefoot would make some noise.” Afraid of worsening Uncle Wong’s trauma, Chen Ge kept his darker suspicion to himself.

“Perhaps.” Uncle Wong had never solved that mystery. “The white figure turned and ran when she saw me. Once she fled, I wasn’t as frightened, so I chased her. After a while, I saw her enter the woman’s apartment. By the time I reached it, the door was locked.

“The tenant she harassed called the police. When they forced the door open, the apartment was empty. They questioned me, but I had questions of my own. I had waited outside from the moment the white figure entered until the police arrived. No one came out.

“The woman returned the next day and told the police she had spent the night with a friend.” Bitterness entered Uncle Wong’s voice. “They locked me up overnight because of it. I told the truth, but no one believed me.”

Chen Ge sympathized. Anyone would be shaken by such an encounter. He had reacted much the same the first time, though repeated exposure had gradually hardened him.

“Did you see the figure’s face? Did you notice any distinguishing features?” Uncle Wong had given Chen Ge an unexpected opening. Finding a lead so soon after arriving was fortunate.

“I was terrified. Do you think I stopped to study her appearance?” Uncle Wong’s wrinkled face tightened, making him look suddenly older.

“Fang Hwa Apartments is one of Jiujiang’s better residential complexes. Did your cameras never capture the white figure?” Chen Ge hoped the footage might reveal something.

“When the haunting rumors began, the landlord and tenants discussed installing cameras throughout the building. Neither side wanted to pay, so they installed only one, on the woman’s floor.”

“One is better than none. Did it capture anything?” Chen Ge’s curiosity deepened.

“Whether because of a technical fault or something else, the camera goes offline at midnight every night and restores itself ten minutes later. No one has ever explained why.” Uncle Wong checked his phone. “Everything I’ve told you is true, and I told the police the same thing yesterday. It’s late. I should go.”

Uncle Wong was clearly trying to escape the conversation.

“One moment. What apartment did the woman live in?” Chen Ge blocked his path.

“I’m not joking. Even now, I won’t patrol that floor. Nearly every other tenant there has moved out,” Uncle Wong warned him. “The police came yesterday. Until they reach a conclusion, you should leave it alone.”

He walked out with a strangely stiff gait. Near the door, he beckoned Xiao Gu over, whispered something in his ear, and finally left.

“I know. Don’t worry.” After seeing Uncle Wong off, Gu Feiyu returned and rolled his eyes at Chen Ge, who was still standing there. “Our captain said we’re not to admit suspicious people.”

“Do I look like someone suspicious?” Chen Ge leaned toward the window of the room. “Do you think what Uncle Wong said is real?”

“No idea. I’m new,” Gu Feiyu answered honestly. He was far easier to question than Uncle Wong.

“You’re new?” Chen Ge’s eyes shifted. “They hired you for the night patrol, but did they tell you why your predecessor left? Could it be connected to the haunting?”

Gu Feiyu had been writing in a notebook, but his pen froze. “What do you mean?”

“When did you find out about the haunting?”

“Yesterday, when the police came to ask about that woman. I was beside Uncle Wong when he told them the story.”

“It sounds as though they tricked you into taking this job. The management is terrible. You patrol alone at night—aren’t they worried something might happen?” Never one to ignore an injustice, Chen Ge continued, “How about this? I won’t ask you to break any rules, but take my number. If anything strange happens on patrol tonight, call me. I’ll do everything I can to help, so please don’t refuse my goodwill.”

“Goodwill? Where? I don’t see any.” After a little more persuasion, Gu Feiyu finally exchanged numbers with him. “Remember to call me if you run into danger tonight.”

Chen Ge then circled to Fang Hwa Apartments’ back entrance and strolled inside as though he belonged there.

The old guard will never tell me her address. It looks like I’ll have to trouble Wang Xin’s mother.

Approaching the three newer buildings, Chen Ge noticed something he had missed on his first visit. Together, they formed the Chinese character ‘品’, just like the three buildings at the Jiujiang Third Psychological Convalescence Centre.

He headed for the third building—not by choice, but because Wang Xin’s family lived there. “Building Three, fourteenth floor.”

Night had fallen. The moment Chen Ge entered, he felt that the building was colder than the air outside. The lobby stood empty. Beside the elevator, he watched the floor indicator rise and fall.

The building had twenty-three floors, yet the display contained twenty-four numbers. Chen Ge could not tell what the extra one represented. When the indicator reached thirteen, it paused for ten seconds before moving again. Someone had entered the elevator on the thirteenth floor.

Soon the doors opened, and a tall, stylish woman in red heels stepped out. A mask and cap concealed her face like a celebrity avoiding attention.
